channel.title: The Moscow Times - Independent News From Russia
channel.description: The Moscow Times offers everything you need to know about Russia: Breaking news, top stories, business, analysis, opinion, multimedia

item.title: Ukrainian Attacks Kill 2 in Belgorod and Target Wildberries Warehouse in Urals
item.description: Wildberries suspended operations and evacuated workers at its local logistics facility in the city of Yekaterinburg.

item.title: Major Russian Black Sea Oil Terminal Halts Operations Amid Ukrainian Drone Threat
item.description: The Sheskharis terminal in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk has not loaded any tankers since Tuesday morning, Bloomberg reported.

item.title: 'Chastity or Passion?': Orthodox Priests Bring ‘Chastity Lessons’ to Russian Schools
item.description: Amid Russia's demographic crisis, priests lead classes on abstinence before marriage, discourage abortion and reinforce "traditional family values."

item.title: Wildberries Freezes Loan Repayments for Merchants After Drone Strikes
item.description: The three-month payment pause will apply automatically through the company’s in-house financial services through the end of October.

item.title: Putin Visits Siberian Factory Producing Delayed Russian Airliner
item.description: The Kremlin said Vladimir Putin toured the Irkutsk Aviation Plant, which is producing Russia’s long-delayed MC-21 passenger jet.

item.title: Russia Bans Armenian Dairy Imports Over Alleged Health Violations
item.description: The ban follows a raft of Russian restrictions on the import and transit of Armenian food products this summer.

item.title: Russian Central Bank Warns of Higher Inflation as It Lowers Key Rate to 14%
item.description: The modest decrease comes despite concerns that Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries and commercial sites will fuel a renewed inflation surge.

item.title: Where Can Russian Athletes Compete After the IOC’s Provisional Ban Lift?
item.description: The Moscow Times has compiled a list detailing where and how Russian athletes can currently compete on the international stage.

item.title: Russia Among Dozens of Countries Targeted by New Trump Tariffs
item.description: The White House accused Russia and other countries of failing to enact or effectively enforce bans on goods produced with forced labor.

item.title: At Least 6 Dead After Ukrainian Drones Hit Wildberries Warehouses and Industrial Facility
item.description: The online retailer said its logistics centers in St. Petersburg and the Leningrad region, as well as in annexed Crimea, were hit overnight.

item.title: Regions Calling: Russia’s Independent Candidates Face Their Toughest Election Yet
item.description: Many Russians are frustrated with the war and the economy. Can this help candidates trying to challenge the political status quo?

item.title: Kazakhstan Cuts Oil Production Following Drone Strikes on Black Sea Tankers
item.description: Russia has accused Ukraine of targeting oil tankers off its southern Black Sea coast to disrupt the global energy market.

item.title: Warplane Crashes During Training Flight in Moscow Region
item.description: The pilot ejected safely from the unarmed aircraft, military officials told state media.

item.title: Communist Party Official Killed in Ukrainian Drone Attack in Belgorod
item.description: Alexander Logvinov, who headed the Communist Party’s Belgorod city branch, was killed on Tuesday, party officials said.

item.title: Rubio Says U.S. Remains Committed to Ukraine Peace Talks After Meeting With Lavrov
item.description: Rubio said President Donald Trump had made clear that the United States was prepared to help facilitate an end to a "senseless war" if the opportunity arose.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Urges Citizens in Russia to Exercise Caution Following Drone Attacks on Wildberries Warehouses
item.description: Two Kyrgyz citizens were among more than 70 people injured over the weekend during Ukrainian attacks on Wildberries facilities.

item.title: EU Agrees 21st Sanctions Package Against Russia
item.description: Greece received an exemption allowing its shipping firms to continue transporting Russian liquefied natural gas from the Arctic.

item.title: 3 Killed as Wave of Ukrainian Drones Strikes Southern Russia and Crimea
item.description: In Voronezh, falling drone debris triggered a fire at a residence that killed a three-year-old boy, local officials said.

item.title: German Nuclear Fuel Plant Cleared to Work With Russia's Rosatom
item.description: There is so far no EU agreement on an extension of sanctions on Russia to the nuclear power sector.

item.title: Yandex Market Limits Liability for Drone Attacks After Wildberries Strikes
item.description: The changes make Yandex Market the latest major Russian marketplace to shift more of the financial risk from wartime disruptions onto merchants.

item.title: Richest United Russia Candidates Report More Than $103M in Combined Income
item.description: The combined income of the seven richest United Russia candidates exceeded the annual budgets of several regional capitals.

item.title: Russia Says It Struck Ukrainian Ports and Ships
item.description: The Defense Ministry said it struck port infrastructure and vessels in the cities of Odesa and Chornomorsk that it said were supporting the Ukrainian military.

item.title: European Forces Intercept ‘Shadow Fleet’ Oil Tanker in Mediterranean Sea
item.description: A European naval mission boarded a Russia-linked oil tanker suspected of sailing under a false flag on Monday, the EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas said.

item.title: State Duma Passes ‘Civic Death’ Bills Cutting Off Exiled Critics From Banking and Consular Services
item.description: Rights advocates warn that the legislation extends the Russian government’s ability to punish dissent far beyond its borders.

item.title: Lavrov and Rubio Set to Meet at ASEAN Summit to Discuss Ukraine Peace Talks
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he would also discuss broader bilateral issues with Russia’s foreign minister on Thursday.

item.title: Russia Issues Arrest Warrant for Ukraine’s New Military Commander Just Hours After Appointment
item.description: The arrest warrant appeared just hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky dismissed General Oleksandr Syrskyi and named Mykhailo Drapatyi as his replacement.

item.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Wildberries Logistics Hubs in Southern Russia
item.description: The founder of the online retailer said overnight attacks hit two distribution centers in the Krasnodar and Stavropol regions.

item.title: Azerbaijan Hosted Secret Russian-German Talks, President Aliyev Says
item.description: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev claimed the meeting was held without his knowledge but said he could “only welcome it” if it could help end the Ukraine war.

item.title: Russia’s Fuel Market Partially ‘Stabilizing,’ Deputy PM Novak Says
item.description: Novak said state measures like foreign fuel purchases and delayed routine refinery maintenance have helped relieve pressure on the domestic market.

item.title: Should Russia Brace for a New Mobilization?
item.description: Questions are once again mounting over whether the Kremlin could resort to a politically costly mobilization to boost its manpower.

item.title: Yabloko Candidates Disqualified in St. Petersburg Elections Over Missing Paperwork
item.description: Members of Yabloko told local media that 11 of their 25 nominees received formal notices claiming their submissions were incomplete.

item.title: FBI Director Kash Patel Plans Trip to Russia in October – Politico
item.description: The Kremlin declined to confirm or deny the trip, telling reporters that “these kinds of visits usually happen behind closed doors.”

item.title: India Summons Russian Envoy Over Killing of 4 Indian Sailors
item.description: Ukraine said Russia hit a cargo ship with three cruise missiles on Sunday, killing 10 people including four Indian citizens.

item.title: Russia Expels Italian Diplomats in Tit-for-Tat Move
item.description: The expulsion of two Italian diplomats comes after Rome expelled a pair of Russian diplomats who were accused of spying.

item.title: State Duma Expected to Vote on Updated Bill Cutting Off Exiled Critics From Banking and Property Services, Report Says
item.description: The State Duma previously passed a milder version of the bill — which included basic asset freezes and the denial of consular services — in its first reading last December.

item.title: What We Know About the Aftermath of Ukraine’s Wildberries Drone Strikes
item.description: The strikes, one of the costliest attacks on Russia’s commercial infrastructure since the start of the war, hit small businesses especially hard.

item.title: 5 Killed in Drone Attack on Bus Near Ukrainian Border, Belgorod Governor Says
item.description: Acting Belgorod region Governor Alexander Shuvayev said 23 people in total were injured in the daytime strike.

item.title: Russia Extends Visa-Free Travel for Chinese Tourists
item.description: The waiver, which reciprocates China’s visa-free regime for Russians, is now set to expire in December 2027.

item.title: Russian Army Restored Control Over Key Supply Highway to Crimea, Official Claims
item.description: Kyiv has vowed to “isolate” Crimea from mainland Russia by taking control of the R-280 highway in occupied southern Ukraine.

item.title: Chelyabinsk Activist Ends Election Bid After Jump From Window to Escape Police
item.description: Mikhail Popov fractured his spine and was hospitalized last week after jumping out of a second-floor window while attempting to flee visiting police officers at his home.

item.title: Moscow Judge Orders Detention of Space Researcher on Treason Allegations
item.description: Maxim Kravchuk, an aerodynamics specialist, works at the Central Research Institute of Machine Building, a Moscow-based research institution operating under the state space agency Roscosmos, Russian media reported.

item.title: Overnight Ukrainian Attacks Across Russia Kill At Least 4
item.description: Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted nearly 400 Ukrainian drones between Sunday night and Monday morning.

item.title: Nadezhdin Says His Political Campaign Is Over Amid Kremlin Pressure
item.description: “I no longer have any opportunity to engage in opposition politics legally in Russia," the politician said.

item.title: Russia Hits Ukraine With Largest Number of Ballistic Missiles, Kyiv Says
item.description: Russian forces have stepped up ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv and other cities in recent weeks.

item.title: Ukrainian Drone Attacks Kill 7 Warehouse Workers in Russia
item.description: A wave of Ukrainian drones struck two warehouses belonging to the online retailer Wildberries, as well as an oil refinery in the Moscow region.

item.title: Could Russia's Wartime Debt Boom Trigger a Banking Crisis?
item.description: Banks are increasingly exposed as high interest rates and slowing growth make it harder for companies and households to repay their debts.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Russia to Restore Direct Flights Halted After Deadly Plane Crash
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said that both countries have now “resolved all issues” connected to the downing of an Azerbaijani passenger jet in late 2024.

item.title: Kremlin Rejects Trump’s Election Interference Claim
item.description: “Russia has never interfered in the domestic affairs of other countries,” top spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

item.title: A Lawmaker Said a Domestic Violence Law Would Undermine Families. Then Came the Backlash.
item.description: Women have taken to social media to criticize State Duma lawmaker Nina Ostanina's claim that a domestic violence law would discourage men from marrying.

item.title: Moscow Region Court Fines Nadezhdin $13 for ‘Extremist’ Navalny Photo
item.description: The conviction means Nadezhdin is now banned from collecting signatures to appear on the ballot for State Duma elections this September.
